Subject: Observability add-ons: retention, tracing, dashboards — pricing & scope confirmation

Hi Ami / PulseHealth team,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation I attached a concise pricing workbook (observability-pricing-v3.xlsx) that translates the add-on SKUs we discussed into a sample committed package. Key points to confirm:

- Retention: 90-day hot retention vs 365-day tiered (hot/warm/cold) — pricing shown per GB-month for each tier.
- Tracing: ingest volume vs indexed traces; we modeled a 2M spans/day baseline with 10% indexed sampling.
- Advanced dashboards: seat-based + per-query metering in heavy-export scenarios (see sheet "Dashboards").

We recommended a 12-month committed path with a pilot window (3 months) at a locked pilot rate and a staged discount once you convert to annual commit. The workbook contains example breakpoints at $25k, $75k, and $200k ARR for add-ons; the commercial team (cc'd) can map a bespoke concession for the PulseHealth case.

Ask: can you confirm which retention band you expect to use for logs (90 / 180 / 365) and whether traces should be billed on ingest or on indexed traces for your compliance team? Once I have that I can produce an SOW and an invoice for procurement.

Attachments: observability-pricing-v3.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Irene Choi

Irene — thanks, this is helpful. Couple of clarifying items from our side:

1) Retention: Primary ask is 180-day hot retention for logs, but we may archive to cold storage beyond that. Is the 180-day row in your sheet the "hot" tier or the middle band? We want to avoid surprise egress charges when pulling data into our analytics.
2) Tracing: Our SREs want index-on-write for critical services (user-auth, payment). Can you call out a per-indexed-trace cost vs raw ingest?
3) Dashboards: We'll need 6 product seats and 3 admin seats initially. What happens if we exceed query thresholds during spikes — do you throttle or bill overage?

Procurement note: we'll need your standard SOW + vendor questionnaire; Samir is leading the procurement checklist. If you can send the SOW draft and a short summary of SOC2/compliance posture that will accelerate internal review.

Hi Ami — thanks for the quick feedback. I pulled the numbers into the body here so it's easier to scan:

- Retention pricing (example):
  * 90-day hot: $0.35 / GB-month
  * 180-day hot: $0.28 / GB-month (you asked about this — it's our mid band; cold archival beyond 180d is $0.06 / GB-month)
- Tracing: ingest pricing is $0.12 / 1k spans; indexed traces are an additional $0.45 / 1k indexed traces. For key services you outlined we recommend indexing only 5–15% of spans.
- Dashboards: seat pricing is $125 / seat / month for product seats; admin seats $225 / seat / month. Query overage: we include a monthly free tier of 100k heavy queries; above that we bill $0.0015 / query or we can set an enforced soft-throttle with alerts if you'd prefer predictable spend.

Discount / commitment mechanics (proposal):
- Pilot (3 months): locked pilot rates = list rates above with a 10% pilot discount; no long-term commitment required.
- Annual commit conversion: one-time conversion credit equal to 50% of pilot spend applied pro rata to the first invoice after signing a 12-month commitment.
- Additional concession: for a >=$75k ARR add-on commit we can apply a further 12% commercial discount (subject to legal approval).

If PulseHealth is comfortable with the pilot approach we can: (1) update the SOW to call out the 180-day hot retention band, (2) itemize the indexed-trace counts for the three critical services you mentioned, and (3) lock the six product / three admin seats for the pilot period.

Irene and Marcus — can one of you prepare the pilot SOW & a short compliance snapshot (SOC2 + data handling notes) for Samir and procurement?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai
